empezando.bajada: Animated Lucide icons on native Web Animations API. Zero animation dependencies at runtime — no @angular/animations, no Motion, no GSAP.

instalar.texto: Angular 20, 21, or 22 (peerDependencies: >=20.0.0 <23.0.0). The only real dependency is tslib. MIT licensed.

primerIcono.texto1: The component is standalone: import it where you use it, no intermediate module. The icon is passed as a value, via a named import.

porQue.texto1: Because it's the path that actually tree-shakes. The numbers come from the budget that runs in CI on every commit, not a promise:
porQue.filaSolo: Just the component, no icon at all
porQue.texto2: An icon costs that icon. Looking one up by name at runtime forces the bundler to keep all 1767, because it can't know which one you'll ask for.

nameOptIn.texto1: It exists, and it's opt-in on purpose: without registering the catalog, name="bell" renders nothing and doesn't throw — same contract as an unknown name.
nameOptIn.nota: That provideIconCatalog(ANIMATED_ICONS) is exactly what pulls in the 94 KB. Use it when the icon name is data (it comes from an API, from config), not when you write it yourself in the template.

trigger.group: Draws on mount and animates with the hover of the nearest .group container — the same one Tailwind's group-hover: uses. If there's none, it listens to the icon itself.
trigger.view: On entering the viewport. viewOnce decides once vs. every re-entry.
trigger.manual: Never on its own: you trigger it by calling play() on the instance.

velocidad.texto1: One multiplier for every computed duration — choreography and morph transitions alike. 1 means no change; without providing anything, behavior stays untouched.
velocidad.texto2: The speed chips in this site's top bar are exactly that, live. They apply starting with the next playback: whatever's already running keeps the duration the browser already gave it.

morph.texto1: Lives in a separate entry point, glyphflow/morph, so that anyone who only wants animated icons doesn't pay for shape-interpolation math.
morph.nota: The first value renders static — morphing "from nothing" doesn't exist. SSR and any browser without WAAPI fall into the same case: you see the icon, it just doesn't animate.
morph.texto2: [spring] decides what the transition feels like: smooth (default, no overshoot), snappy (fast, subtle overshoot), or bouncy (overshoots the target and settles back). The spring never touches the geometry — only the duration and how keyframes are spaced out over time. It also accepts your own { k, c } if you want to tune it yourself.

accesibilidad.bajada: Two decisions, both made so you never have to combine flags: an icon is decorative or semantic, and reduced motion means different things on an icon than on a morph.

regla.texto1: You never coordinate aria-hidden with aria-label. You either set label, or you don't:

filaDecorativo.cuando: The icon sits next to text that already says the same thing.

filaSemantico.cuando: The icon is the content: a button with no text.

regla.texto2: decorative defaults to true and you almost never touch it: label is what decides. Applies the same way to <gf-icon> and <gf-icon-morph>.

reducedMotion.texto1: Both components respect it by default (respectReducedMotion = true). But respecting it doesn't mean the same thing in both, and that difference is deliberate, not an inheritance oversight:

icono.texto: The choreography is decoration on top of an icon that's already the right one. Removing the motion doesn't remove information: the bell is still a bell.

morph.titulo: In <gf-icon-morph>: it jumps to the new icon
morph.texto: Here, staying still would leave the user looking at the wrong icon. The destination isn't decoration, it's state: if the button went from "play" to "pause", it has to show "pause".

reducedMotion.nota: Reduced motion is respected by removing the movement, not the state change. The morph skips the transition and paints the destination immediately.
reducedMotion.override: If you need to ignore the system preference — a rare case, and justifying it is on you — the override exists: [respectReducedMotion]="false".

motionLint.titulo: How the catalog’s motion is kept cheap
motionLint.texto1: Every curated choreography is analysed by a deterministic linter — the same Motion Inspector you can open on any icon in the catalog, running as a CI check over the whole curated set on any PR that touches it. One implementation, two places.
motionLint.texto2: It reports three things, measured over 911 icons and 2236 variants:
motionLint.animaD: Animating d — this fails the build. Changing the path data redraws it every frame; transform and opacity are moved by the compositor without repainting. The catalog has zero of these today, so the rule guards against a regression rather than flagging existing debt. Progressive stroke (autoDraw) is exempt: there is no cheap equivalent for it.
motionLint.duracion: Duration over 1200 ms — a warning. 53 variants exceed it, mostly icons that tell a small story (dice rolling, weather).
motionLint.rotacion: Rotation over 720° — a warning. Exactly two: orbit and calendar-cog/spin, both deliberate.
motionLint.porQueAvisa: Only the first one breaks the build. The other two measure cost, not correctness, and an expensive choreography can be the right call for a given icon — a check that fails on a matter of taste gets switched off within a week.

noDecide.titulo: What the component doesn't decide for you
noDecide.color: Color. The SVG uses stroke="currentColor", so it inherits the text color. Contrast against the background is on you.
noDecide.area: Touch target. size is the size of the drawing. An icon button needs its own padding to reach the 24×24 CSS px minimum target.
noDecide.foco: Focus. The icon isn't interactive: it never receives focus or keyboard input. If it sits inside something clickable, that something has to be a real <button> or <a>.

ssr.bajada: glyphflow renders on the server without a real window or document. The icon arrives already painted in the HTML; the animation starts once the browser hydrates.

filaServidor.queSeVe: The full <svg>, with its geometry and its aria-hidden. No animation: there's no WAAPI in Node.

filaHidratar.queSeVe: The same SVG, now alive. The trigger starts working.

ssr.sinParpadeo: No flicker, no layout shift: the SVG the server paints is the exact same node the client animates. It's never replaced — animations are just added on top.

sinConfig.texto: No afterNextRender, no isPlatformBrowser guard, no deferred import of the component. It works with whatever SSR config you already have.

verificacion.texto1: With a smoke test that runs in real Node, not jsdom — and that's the point: jsdom defines window, so a test running there wouldn't prove anything. The script starts by deliberately failing if it detects window:
verificacion.texto2: Then it renders with renderApplication from @angular/platform-server and demands two things from the resulting HTML: that there's an <svg>, and that it carries the decorative icon's aria-hidden="true". Runs in CI on every commit (npm run test:ssr).
verificacion.nota: The second check isn't decoration. A render that "doesn't throw" but returns empty HTML passes any test that only checks for an exception — that's why the test asserts on content, not on the absence of an error.

morphServidor.texto: <gf-icon-morph> falls through the same path as the client's first render: it paints the static icon. Morphing "from nothing" doesn't exist, and on the server there's no previous value to morph from either. You see the right icon; the transition waits for the browser.

api.bajada: The whole public surface, across two entry points. This page renders from the same list a test compares against the package's real exports — if it documented something that no longer exists, the test fails.

metodos.intro: Public methods on the component instance. They're what you need with trigger="manual":
metodos.play: play(variant?) — plays a variant; with no argument, the one from the animation input.
metodos.reverse: reverse() — returns to the starting pose animating, not all at once. Tracks only: reversing an autoDraw would UNdraw the icon, which is nobody's intent when the pointer leaves.
metodos.cancel: cancel() — cuts everything off and puts the shapes back in their original pose.

iconos.texto: On top of the above, glyphflow exports one const per icon with an Icon suffix — bellIcon, trash2Icon, circleCheckIcon. That's the tree-shakeable path, which is why they're not listed one by one: there are ~1767 of them, and the browsable catalog lives at the icons page.
iconos.nota: The const's name is the icon's name in camelCase plus Icon: trash-2 → trash2Icon, circle-check → circleCheckIcon. Each icon's detail panel gives you the snippet already built.

inputsIcono.iconDef: The tree-shakeable path. Wins over name.
inputsIcono.name: Requires provideIconCatalog. Unknown = renders nothing, doesn't throw.
inputsIcono.loop: With one-shot easings, the cut between loops shows.
inputsIcono.delay: Extra delay (ms), ADDED on top of each track's own.
inputsIcono.label: With label, the icon is semantic.
inputsIcono.respectReducedMotion: Stays static if the system asks for it.

inputsMorph.icon: The binding IS the state. The first value renders static.
inputsMorph.label: With label, the icon is semantic.
inputsMorph.respectReducedMotion: Here it JUMPS to the destination instead of staying still.
inputsMorph.spring: smooth / snappy / bouncy, or your own { k, c }. Only decides timing, never geometry.

simbolos.provideGfIcons: Optional global config. Today just durationScale.
simbolos.GF_ICONS_CONFIG: The InjectionToken behind provideGfIcons, in case you want to provide it yourself.
simbolos.provideIconCatalog: Registers the catalog so you can use name=. Opt-in: without this, name= renders nothing.
simbolos.GF_ICON_CATALOG: The catalog's token. Without it, an unknown name renders empty, without throwing.
simbolos.GENERATED_ICONS: The remaining {{generados}} from Lucide, auto-draw only.
simbolos.ANIMATED_ICONS: Curated + generated. Referencing it anchors the whole catalog in your bundle.
simbolos.ANIMATED_ICON_NAMES: The catalog's keys. Same bundle cost as ANIMATED_ICONS.
simbolos.ICON_ALIASES: Real Lucide renames (same glyph, new name).
simbolos.resolveIconName: Applies the aliases: old name → current name.
simbolos.ICON_META: Per-icon metadata: curated flag, source, search tags.
simbolos.ICON_TAGS: Lucide's search synonyms per icon, without the geometry.
simbolos.morphKeyframes: Computes the discrete `d` keyframes between two icons. Doesn't animate anything.
simbolos.runMorph: morphKeyframes + element.animate(). Returns the Animation so you can control it.
simbolos.canonicalD: The already-resolved `d` of an icon — what renders when there's no transition.
simbolos.morphAt: The exact morph pose at any t (0-1), with no animation — for scrubbers and manual control.
simbolos.createLiveMorph: The live engine: a spring driven by requestAnimationFrame, instead of precomputed WAAPI keyframes.
simbolos.SPRING_PRESETS: smooth (ζ=1.00), snappy (ζ=0.73), and bouncy (ζ=0.40). The last two actually overshoot.
simbolos.STEPS_DEFAULT: 20 discrete poses. Decided in the Lab by comparing 10/15/20/30.
simbolos.SPRING_TAIL_DEFAULT: What to do with the spring's asymptotic tail.
simbolos.PASOS_DEFAULT: 20 discrete poses. Decided in the Lab by comparing 10/15/20/30.
simbolos.COLA_DEFAULT: What to do with the spring's asymptotic tail.

tipos.AnimatedIconDef: An icon: geometry + its animation variants.
tipos.IconChoreography: A variant: per-shape tracks + autoDraw + reverseOnLeave.
tipos.MotionTrack: Keyframes + WAAPI options for one shape.
tipos.IconMeta: One catalog icon's metadata. `tags` is always populated.
tipos.MorphIcon: What [icon] accepts: an AnimatedIconDef or its geometry.
tipos.RunMorphOpts: The above + loop, direction, and durationScale.
tipos.LiveMorphOpts: spring and durationScale, same vocabulary as the baked engine.

migracion.bajada: glyphflow renamed its public surface in v2. The old names still work — this page says what changed, and until when.

v2.texto: One thing: the prefix. Everything called Max* is now Gf*, and the elements <max-icon> / <max-icon-morph> are <gf-icon> / <gf-icon-morph>. The package is called glyphflow, so the brand is one word, not two. No behaviour changed with the rename.

renombres.texto: Every row on the left still resolves to the one on the right — they are the same object, not a copy. That matters for GF_ICONS_CONFIG in particular: two distinct injection tokens would not see each other, and a provideMaxIcons() would silently never reach the component.

deprecados.titulo: How long the old names last
deprecados.texto: They are exported and marked @deprecated through the whole v2 line, and they go away in v3. Nothing breaks by upgrading to v2 — you can rename at your own pace.
deprecados.nota: A rename of a selector does not behave like a rename of a symbol: if a symbol disappears, TypeScript shouts. If a selector disappears, a template is just text — Angular treats the unknown element as nothing and renders it. Silently. That is why the old selectors stay.

comparativa.bajada: Measured, not claimed. Numbers below come from a real production build, and the method is written down so you can redo it.

peso.texto: Net cost over an empty Angular 22 app, gzip, entry chunks only. Measured on 2026-08-24 against the versions listed.
peso.lottieNota: the player alone, before a single animation
peso.lectura: Read the last column, not the first. glyphflow has the highest floor — it ships an animation engine — and the lowest slope: each extra animated icon costs less than each extra static icon from the others. The lines cross around 30 icons against @ng-icons and around 80 against @lucide/angular. Below that, they are lighter, and this page says so.

metodo.texto: A clean app from ng new --minimal on Angular 22, one component importing one icon from each library, ng build --configuration production, gzip of the entry chunks, minus the same build with no icon library at all. Same harness for every row.
metodo.cicatriz: An earlier attempt measured the published bundles directly with esbuild instead of building the app. It reported 241 KB for one @lucide/angular icon — 25× off. Angular's own optimizer prunes it fine; esbuild could not, because that package ships no @__PURE__ annotations. The wrong number was never published, and this note is here so nobody re-derives it that way.

verificar.bajada: Do not take the numbers on this site on faith. Here is how to get them in your own project.

porQue.texto: Because "tree-shakeable" is a claim, and yours is the only bundle that matters. A library can be perfectly tree-shakeable and still land whole in your build — one import * as, one lookup by string, one barrel file, and the bundler stops being able to prove what is unused.

como.texto1: Build twice and subtract. First, ng build --configuration production as you have it today; note the gzip size of the entry chunks. Then add the icon and build again. The difference is what the icon cost you — not what anyone promised.
como.texto2: To see why a number is what it is, build with --stats-json and open the result in any bundle analyser. What you are looking for is whether the icon catalog appears whole: if you imported bellIcon and the output mentions icons you never named, something is anchoring the registry.
como.texto3: The usual culprit is name="bell" with provideIconCatalog(ANIMATED_ICONS). That path is a convenience and it is documented as such: a lookup by string cannot be tree-shaken, so it pulls the whole catalog on purpose. If you want the small number, pass the icon by value with [iconDef].

esperar.texto: Measured in CI on every push against the published package:
esperar.uno: One icon — around 13.7 KB gzip net over an empty app, engine included.
esperar.diez: Ten icons — around 15.2 KB. The engine is paid once; each icon adds roughly 0.17 KB.
esperar.catalogo: The whole catalog via name= — over 100 KB. That is the trade, and it is the reason the catalog is opt-in.
esperar.nota: If your numbers are far above these, the difference is in your build, not in the package — and the stats file will say where.

problemas.bajada: Four things that look like bugs and usually are not.

noAnima.titulo: The icon renders but never animates
noAnima.texto: In order of how often it turns out to be each one:
noAnima.reducido: The system asks for reduced motion. Icons respect prefers-reduced-motion by default and stay on their base pose. That is the intended behaviour — check your OS setting before anything else.
noAnima.trigger: The trigger never fires. The default is hover. With trigger="manual" nothing happens until you call play() yourself, and with trigger="group" the animation hangs off an ancestor being hovered, not the icon.
noAnima.variante: The variant does not exist on that icon. Asking for animation="spin" on an icon that only has default and draw is a no-op, not an error. Every icon in the catalog lists its variants.

morphRaro.texto: Morphing pairs subpaths by proximity. When two icons share nothing structural — a circle and a bell, say — there is no good pairing to find, and the result is honest about it: shapes travel across the canvas in ways nobody designed. This is a limit of shape interpolation, not a defect.
morphRaro.queHacer: What helps: morph between icons of the same family (bell → bell-ring), or between shapes with the same number of subpaths. The Lab lets you try any pair before you commit to it.

nameVacio.texto: The catalog is opt-in. Without provideIconCatalog(ANIMATED_ICONS) in your providers, name="bell" has nothing to look up and the component renders empty — deliberately, because registering 1767 icons by default would put the entire catalog in every bundle. Either add the provider, or pass the icon by value with [iconDef].

ssr.titulo: Server rendering fails or does not hydrate
ssr.texto: There is nothing to configure — no afterNextRender, no isPlatformBrowser guard, no deferred import. If your build fails at render time, the cause is almost never the icon: the component touches no browser global on the server, and that is verified in CI on every commit with a smoke test that runs in real Node, not jsdom.
ssr.nota: The SVG the server paints is the exact same node the client animates — it is never replaced, animations are just added on top. If you see a flash, look for something else swapping the DOM.

temas.bajada: Icons inherit. That single decision answers most theming questions before you ask them.

color.texto: The SVG uses stroke="currentColor", so the icon takes the text color of whatever contains it. There is no color input, and that is on purpose: an input would be a second source of truth that drifts from the CSS around it.
color.consecuencia: The consequence is convenient — change the container's color and the icon follows, including on hover, on focus, and inside a disabled button — and it is also the whole of the API. If you need a color the container does not have, set color on the icon in CSS like any other element.

oscuro.texto: Nothing to do. If your text is readable in both themes, so is the icon: it is the same color. That holds for any mechanism — a class on <html>, a data attribute, prefers-color-scheme — because the icon never reads the theme, only its inherited color.
oscuro.nota: Contrast is still yours to check. Inheriting the text color means inheriting its contrast problems too: an icon at 3:1 against the background fails the same threshold a graphic element has to meet.

trazo.texto: The default strokeWidth is 2, drawn in a 24-unit viewBox. Rendered at 24 px that is a clean 2 px line. Rendered at 16 px it is 1.33 px, and on a non-retina screen that lands between pixels and reads blurry.
trazo.recomendacion: Below 20 px, drop to [strokeWidth]="1.5". Above 32 px you can go the other way — 2 keeps looking thin as the icon grows. The value is an input precisely because the right answer depends on the size you render at, and only you know that.
